answer: An odds comparison site shows the price every sportsbook is offering on the same outcome, side by side, so you can bet it where it pays most. It is the single biggest improvement a bettor can make: the gap between the best and worst price on an ordinary NFL side is often 5 to 10 cents, which is more than the vig. The limits are that most sites show sportsbooks only (not exchanges or prediction markets), lag the real price by seconds to minutes, and cannot place the bet, so the number is often gone by the time you open the book.

sections.h2: What a comparison site shows you

blocks.p: A grid: outcomes down the side, venues across the top, a price in each cell, and the best price highlighted. Good sites add the no-vig fair price derived from a sharp book, the implied probability, the opening line and how it has moved, and alerts when a price moves or a gap opens.

list: Coverage. Most grids are sportsbooks. In 2026 the lowest-margin price on a major US game is frequently on Kalshi, Polymarket, Novig or ProphetX, and a site that does not show them is comparing the expensive half of the market.
Latency. Free sites sample prices every few minutes; paid ones every few seconds. Lines on a moving market change faster than that.
The last mile. The site shows -102 at Book X; you open Book X; it is -108. The best price on a screen is a historical fact by the time you act on it.
Fees. A screen compares headline prices. An exchange price at 2.00 with 2% commission and a sportsbook at +100 are not the same; a fee-adjusted comparison is rarer than it should be.
Access. A comparison site can show you Pinnacle's price, but a US bettor cannot bet it.

blocks.callout: The grid is a map of where the money was a few seconds ago. The useful question is where it is now and whether you can get there before it moves.

ol: Pick a reference column (Pinnacle, Circa or a deep exchange) and read every other price relative to it, vig removed.
Only act on gaps larger than the fees and the expected slippage.
Keep accounts funded at the venues that show up most often with the best price, or use a venue that routes from one balance.
Record the price you got, not the price the screen showed; the difference is your execution cost.
Check closing lines afterwards. A screen that keeps finding you prices that beat the close is doing its job.

sections.h2: Comparison site versus a trading terminal

blocks.p: A comparison site is a screen. A trading terminal is a screen attached to an order button and a single balance. The difference is the last mile: the terminal places the bet at the venue with the best fee-adjusted price at the moment you click, from money already there. For a bettor who moves size across several venues, that removes the delay and the account-hopping that eat most of the value a screen finds.

takeaways: Odds comparison is the biggest single improvement most bettors can make; the best-to-worst gap often exceeds the vig.
Most sites compare sportsbooks only; the sharpest prices in 2026 are often on exchanges and prediction markets.
Latency and the last mile cost much of the value: the screen's price is often gone when you reach the book.
Read every price relative to a no-vig reference and act only on gaps bigger than fees plus slippage.
A terminal that compares and executes from one balance closes the gap a screen leaves open.
terminalup: TerminalUp is the comparison and the order in one place. faq.q: What is the best odds comparison site?
faq.a: For a free sportsbook grid, Betstamp, Action Network and Oddschecker. For sharp tools, OddsJam and Unabated. For comparison plus execution across sportsbooks, exchanges and prediction markets, TerminalUp.
Many have free tiers with slower refresh and fewer books. Fast, broad coverage and fair-line tools are paid.

faq.q: Do comparison sites show prediction markets?
faq.a: Mostly not, or only partially. Since the sharpest US prices in 2026 are often on Kalshi, Polymarket, Novig and ProphetX, that is a significant gap.

faq.q: Why is the price gone when I open the sportsbook?
faq.a: Latency. The site sampled the price seconds or minutes ago; the book moved. Faster refresh helps; placing the bet from the same screen removes the problem.

faq.q: How much does line shopping save?
faq.a: Typically 1% to 3% of turnover for a bettor who takes the best price every time, which is more than the margin between a losing and a winning record at -110.

faq.q: Can an odds comparison site place bets for me?
faq.a: Standard sites link you to the book. A cross-venue terminal places the order at the best venue from one balance.
